A clear, lovely chime.

…That light. That sound. Those, at least, he would never forget in all his life.

A bell announcing battle.

The sight of her, making even plain armor ring beautifully.

“—Let me ask you. Are you my Master?”

The words remain clear.

As the image wears away, they stay sharply engraved within him.

…Yes. The contract was complete.

Just as she had chosen him as her master, he had sworn to help her.

Moonlight still shone cold and clear into the darkness.

As though following the knight’s example, the shed returned to its former silence.

晩年の頃。
午睡の間際、ふと、懐かしい剣戟を思い出した。
正しい順番は思い出せない。
記憶は遠く、おぼろになって、あの頃の心の在り方も、今は遠い出来事だ。

pages.en:
Late in life, on the verge of an afternoon nap, he suddenly remembered a familiar clash of swords.

He could no longer put it all in the right order.

The memories were distant, indistinct. Even the shape of his heart in those days was now a thing far away.

「その時は私が死ぬだけでしょう。シロウが傷つく事ではなかった。繰り返しますが、今後あのような行動はしないように。マスターである貴方が私を庇う必要はありませんし、そんな理由もないでしょう」

Let us tell an old story.

The story of him and her, of barely fifteen days spent in pursuit of a Holy Grail.

“Then I alone would have died. There was no reason for you to be hurt.

“I repeat: you must never act that way again. You are my Master. You have neither the need nor any cause to shield me.”

“If they continued forward bearing that absence, only tragedy could await them.”

“Because, for some reason I can’t fathom, other people matter more to you than you do.”

自分一人では誰も救えない。
本当にこの戦いを終わらせるのなら、初めからやるべき事は決まっていたのだ。

He had been a fool.

Alone, he could save no one.

If he truly meant to end this battle, what he had to do had been clear from the start.

A man had asked him:

Would he fight no one, kill no one, let no one be killed?

If he had realized he was wrong, he should first decide what to set right and whom to punish.

Perhaps her soul was still on the battlefield.

Before dawn.

Under an indigo sky, she surrendered herself to the wind and looked only into the distance.

A king is not human.

Happily, the sky was high and the wind cool.

That memory lives on in his heart, still clear and blue.

“King Arthur’s purpose is to obtain the Holy Grail. Even if that is achieved, I will not return to being Altria.

“From the beginning, I have had only one wish.

“Since the moment I took up the sword, this oath has remained unchanging. It always will.”

The girl only wanted to protect everyone.

But to accomplish it, she had to cast away the feeling that made her want to protect them.

…With a human heart, she could not protect the country as its king.

Knowing that, she drew the sword.

Knowing that, she swore to live as king.

However often she was abandoned, feared, betrayed, her heart would not change.

She had surrendered her human heart.

That was the price the young girl had agreed to pay for the chance to protect them.

If anything could be done, it was at least to end it.

To set right the contradiction of corpses being kept alive.

To make the cause of this hell atone for it.

The priest spoke.

The truth of ten years ago. The malice laid within the Holy Grail.

The reality that there was no salvation anywhere.

None of them could be undone.

A Hero of Justice could only tidy up efficiently after the fact.

I have no clear enemy.

I have no wish for myself.

That she could not begin a new life.

That she had duties as king. She had gone on stubbornly refusing.

“Ah—”

…She remembered a distant oath.

One phrase carved into her heart.

…I have chosen to fight.

Even if I lose everything. Even if everyone comes to hate me.

The sun rose.

The still wind began to stir.

Gold that seemed eternal.

Within it—

“There is just one last thing I have to tell you.”

Her voice was strong, full of resolve.

“…Yeah. What is it?”

With all the bravery he could muster, he answered as he always would.

She turned.

“Shirou—I love you.”

She said those words.

The wind blew.

Dazzled by the morning sun, he closed his eyes a little, then opened them.

He was not surprised.

He had felt it would be like this.

The farewell.

The moment she vanished. He had thought it would surely be like this.

Only wilderness filled his sight.

With the passing wind, the knight had vanished.

Just as when she appeared.

Cleanly. Leaving not even a trace of her image.

“Yeah—you really are yourself to the very end.”

No regret in the murmur.

Holding what he had lost and what remained in his heart, he simply narrowed his eyes against the rising light.

A distant land in the light of dawn.

Like the golden meadow she had run across.

It was not a story to tell anyone.

Only a small wish, the kind you might make upon a star.

かけられた時間も、かかげられた理想も、かなえようとした人生も、何かと厄介だったからだろう。
どれほどの道を歩こうと、行程はわずかとも縮まらない。
休まず、諦めず、迷わずに、まなじりを強く絞り。
長い道を、歩いていた。

It was a long journey.

Perhaps because the time it demanded, the ideal he held aloft, and the life he sought to make real were all so troublesome.

However far he walked, the journey did not grow any shorter.

Without rest, without surrender, without hesitation, his eyes set hard—

He walked the long road.

何処に行けば、何をすれば腰を休められるのか。
そんな、一番初めに決めておくべき旅の終わりを、どうにも見つけ損ねたらしい。

His journey went on and on, without end.

The reason was simple.

Where could he go, what could he do, that would let him sit and rest?

The journey’s end, the first thing he should have decided, was the thing he had somehow failed to find.

Nothing lasts forever.

However celebrated a machine may have been in its prime, the more it is used, the more it declines.

Machines, flesh, even the mind: all are the same.

Everything wears away.

With everything it sees, something fades.

And so even a heart that had not thought its task painful would understand, after years of repetition.

Your actions may have meaning.

But you yourself will be worthless to the end.

Hope and disappointment arrive together.

A noble ideal becomes a weary duty, and finally a shabby obsession.

What you looked up to as a child becomes ordinary reality. You may look back at it, but no longer look up.

That is the proper course of a human heart.

But he had never been proper.

So he locked away the very heart that felt the pain, carefully, carefully.

An iron heart—the mark of a tin man.

With this, he could continue his long journey.

Pleasure faded too. Fortunately, he was not greedy. An occasional reward was enough to make him happy.

きっと、彼の旅が終わらなかったのは、目的がなかったからではなく。
本当に見つけたいものを、見つけられなかったから。

He longed for beautiful things.

He saw many people, many towns.

Beautiful things were everywhere.

…Only the light of the star he had parted from that day was nowhere to be found.

Perhaps his journey had not gone on because he lacked a destination.

Perhaps it was because he could not find what he truly wanted to see.

pages.en: But it was a life he could be content with.

永い夢だった。
かけられた呪いも、ささげられた理想も、残してきた結末も、ひどく重いものだったからだろう。
どれほどの眠りを過ごそうと、目覚めは一向に訪れない。
動かず、拒まず、望まずに、深く呼吸を鎮めて。
永い夢に、眠っていた。

pages.en:
It was a long dream.

Perhaps because the curse laid upon her, the ideal she had offered herself to, and the ending she had left behind were all so heavy.

However long she slept, waking never came.

Without moving, without resisting, without wishing, her breathing deep and still—

She slept the long dream.

彼の予言の成就の為、王は死しても剣の以前には戻らない。
時が経って、国が栄えて、人が変わって。

……だって。
彼女はそうである事を引き替えにして、多くの命を預かったのだから。

The king’s duty was not yet over.

To fulfill that prophecy, even in death the king would not return to what she had been before the sword.

Time passed. The country prospered. People changed.

Even if no one wanted a noble king anymore, the oath endured.

…Because she had accepted so many lives into her keeping in exchange for being that king.

でも。

眠りの淵から覗く光景。
今はもう遠い彼の、孤独な道行きにせめて、この心を届けたかった。
人間らしさを仕舞い込んで、同じ事を繰り返すだけの機械になっても。
その痛みに、たとえ誰も気付かなくても。
私がここで、貴方の強さを知っている。

But.

Scenes seen from the edge of sleep.

On his lonely journey, so far away now, she wanted at least to reach him with her voice, with what was in her heart.

Even if he had shut away his humanity and become a machine that only repeated the same act.

Even if no one noticed his pain.

I am here. I know your strength.

過去は変えられないというのなら、それこそが永遠だ。
かつての誓いと覚悟が、王を永遠に繋ぎ止める。
剣以前のカタチに戻る事を、何より本人が許さない。
……でも、会いたかった。
この先、永劫に眠り続ける事になったとしても。
この声を、彼の耳に聞かせたかった。

pages.en:
But there was a promise that lasted forever.

If the past could not be changed, that was eternity.

Her old oath and resolve bound the king forever.

Above all, she herself would not allow a return to the girl she had been before the sword.

…And yet she wanted to see him.

Even if she were to sleep for all eternity after this.

She wanted her voice to reach his ears.

「それは難しいな。そもそも君たちの時間は、絶望的なまでにズレている」
魔術師は言う。
その願いはあまりにも無理があると。
「普通にやったらまず出会えない。実現するには、まあなんていうか、二つの奇跡が必要だ。
一方が待ち続けて、一方が追い続ける。
それもあり得ないと確信しながら、酷く長い時間耐え抜かないといけない。それはほら。言いにくいけど、望むべきではない夢物語だろう？」
魔術師は問う。
そんな事は不可能だと。王の責務など関係なしで、単純に叶うかどうか、望むかどうかという話を。
「ああ、勘違いはしないようにね。王の責任を捨てろって話じゃない。そもそも君は骨の髄まで王さまだ。そんな君から誇りをとったら何も残らない。
君はそのままでいいんだよ。
僕が言っているのは正当な褒美の話だ。小娘一人が幸せに生きる権利。それぐらいの働きは、していると思うんだが」
魔術師は語る。
剣を手に取った時と同じように。
あの時は、これから訪れるであろう苦難を嘲笑い。
今は、叶うかもしれない未来に微笑っている。
返答に意味はない。
これは剣を取る前の少女が、望むか望まないかだけの話。
どちらにしたって彼女に叶える力はない。
なら。
星に願いをかける事と、何の違いがあるだろう
？
「
でも、それが本当にいい事なのかはまた別の話だ。
アルトリア。時代も人も変わっている。あの頃のままなのは君だけだ。
夢は夢のままの方が美しい。君はこのまま、死んだように眠っている方が楽でいい。
それでも
」
応えるまでもない。
口にする事はなくとも、その望みだけは消え去らない。
……逆に言えば、それだけで良かったのだ。
誰も訪れず、ついには誰にも求められず。
人々の幻想から王の姿が消え去るその日まで。
その温かな望みを夢にして、彼女は未来永劫、この眠りに耐えていくのだから。
結局。
彼は生き方を変えられなかったし。
彼女が報われる事も、ついぞありはしなかった。

“That will be difficult. To begin with, your times are hopelessly far apart.”

The mage said her wish asked too much.

“Go about it normally, and you’ll almost certainly never meet. To make it happen—well, how shall I put it? You’ll need two miracles.

“One must go on waiting. The other must go on searching.

“And both must endure for a terribly long time, convinced all the while that it is impossible. You see—I’m sorry to say it, but that’s a fairy tale you really shouldn’t wish for, isn’t it?”

The mage asked.

It was impossible. Never mind a king’s duty; this was simply a question of whether it could come true, and whether she wanted it.

“Oh, don’t misunderstand. I’m not telling you to abandon your responsibilities. You’re a king to your very bones. Take away your pride, and there would be nothing left.

“You may stay exactly as you are.

“I’m talking about a rightful reward. One young girl’s right to live happily. I think you’ve worked hard enough to earn that.”

The mage spoke, just as he had when she took the sword.

Then, he had laughed at the hardships to come.

Now, he smiled at a future that might come true.

Her answer meant nothing.

This was only a question of whether the girl who had not yet taken the sword wanted it.

Either way, she had no power to make it happen.

Then how was it any different from wishing on a star?

“—But whether it would really be a good thing is another matter.

“Altria. The age has changed, and so have its people. Only you remain as you were.

“Dreams are more beautiful as dreams. It would be easier to remain here, sleeping as though dead.

“Even so—”

No answer was needed.

Even unspoken, that wish would not disappear.

…Put another way, that alone was enough.

Until no one came, until no one even wanted her.

Until the king’s image disappeared from human dreams.

Nourished by that warm wish, dreaming it, she would endure this sleep forever.

In the end, he could not change the way he lived.

And she, too, never found her reward.
